1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the manualCode or resetToken against the session's stored values.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because it is tied to a specific session and account identifier.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after a password reset because the session is reset (reset() function clears all session data).

4.why: The website uses HTTPS with TLS (Bun.serve with cert and key).

5.why: Reset codes are cryptographically random (random() function), and user data is not stored in plaintext (bcrypt hashing).

6.why: Email messages (simulated logs) do not expose private user data; only mock codes/URLs are logged.

7.why: User-supplied data (e.g., email, passwords) is validated (validId, validPass) and sanitized (trim, toLowerCase).

8.why: Redirect links are hardcoded to the hospital’s site (/verify route) and not derived from user input.

9.why: Email templates (simulated logs) contain no scripts or HTML from user input; only textContent is used.

10.why: Error pages and logs do not expose user’s private information or tokens (only mock values are logged).

11.why: Passwords and secret codes are stored securely (bcrypt hashes) and not in the code (INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH is pre-hashed).

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials; accounts are pre-defined with hashed passwords.

13.why: The system bars users from making several wrong attempts via throttling (fail() function and attempts Map).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (unknown accounts use a sink to prevent enumeration).

15.why: The password reset code is random (random(18)), complex (base64url), and user-specific (tied to session).
